issue_context.title: RedisCache doesn't implement disposable pattern correctly
comments: I find CA1063 adds a lot of complexity for a scenario (finalizers) that is never recommended (use SafeHandle instead). If the repository doesn't already closely follow this rule, I would suggest disabling it completely and using the simpler pattern of just making `Dispose()` virtual.
@sharwell If there are going to be changes either way, why not satisfy the rule and the framework design guidelines?
Triage: We don't want to turn on CA1063 in this repo. For the most part, we agree with @sharwell comments.

review_comments: This class doesn't implement a finalizer anyway. I'm not sure this change is necessary.

@Pilchie Since this is public and not sealed, wouldn't this be useful if derived types have a finalizer?

(I'm not sure, just asking)

When following the full `IDisposable` pattern from the framework design guidelines, the call to `GC.SuppressFinalize()` is always required. See https://github.com/dotnet/roslyn-analyzers/issues/4745#issuecomment-771833107.
